questions.question:
Choose the correct option to give a one-word substitution for the sentence given:

Killing of an unborn baby.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Foeticide**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Foeticide"** refers to the act of killing an unborn baby or fetus. (भ्रूण हत्या)
 
 
• **Example: **The government has strict laws against foeticide to prevent illegal abortions.

• **Example: **Foeticide is a serious crime in many countries and is punishable under law.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Foeticide**.

• **Paternity **(पितृत्व): The state or quality of being a father.
 
 
• **Example: **A DNA test was conducted to establish paternity in the legal dispute.
 
 
 
• **Maternity **(मातृत्व): The state or quality of being a mother.
 
 
• **Example: **She is on maternity leave after giving birth to her baby.

questions.question:
Select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of idioms/phrases:

Look before you leap.

options.text: Analyze the consequences before making a decision
Depending on others for task completion
Always be humble to people of lower designation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Analyze the consequences before making a decision**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Look before you leap"** means to carefully consider the consequences or outcomes of an action before proceeding. (पहले सोचे, फिर करे)
 
 
• **Example:** Before investing all her savings in the stock market, she remembered the advice to look before she leaped.
 
 
• **Analyze the consequences** implies thinking about possible outcomes of a decision or action before committing to it. (परिणामों का विश्लेषण करना)
 
 
• **Example:** He analyzed the consequences of switching jobs before making the final decision.
 
 
• Hence, **"Analyze the consequences before making a decision"** best expresses the meaning of the idiom **"Look before you leap."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Analyze the consequences before making a decision**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Hide something** (कुछ छुपाना): To keep something hidden or out of sight.
 
 
• **Example:** She tried to hide her disappointment from everyone.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Depending on others for task completion** (दूसरों पर निर्भर होना): Relying on others to complete a task or achieve a goal.
 
 
• **Example:** He is depending on his teammates to finish the project on time.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Always be humble to people of lower designation** (निचले पद के लोगों के प्रति हमेशा विनम्र रहना): To treat people in lower positions with respect and humility.
 
 
• **Example:** A good leader is always humble to people of lower designation.

questions.question:
Choose the option that has an error in the sentence:

"I'm lucky that I have been doing a job I enjoy all my working life."

options.text: I have been doing a job
I enjoy all my working life.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct as written and follows the rules of the **Present Perfect Continuous** tense.
 
• The phrase "**have been doing**" is used correctly to describe an action that started in the past and continues into the present, which is reinforced by the duration "**all my working life**."
 
• The relative clause "**I enjoy**" (modifying "job") is in the simple present tense to indicate a current, ongoing state or preference.
 
• The adverbial of time "**all my working life**" is placed at the end of the sentence to modify the main verb phrase, which is a standard and acceptable structure in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I'm lucky that I have been doing a job I enjoy all my working life."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "I'm lucky that"** – This is a correct introductory phrase. Using "that" to introduce a noun clause is standard.
 
• **Option 2: "I have been doing a job"** – This part is grammatically sound. The use of the continuous form emphasizes the ongoing nature of the career.
 
• **Option 3: "I enjoy all my working life."** – While "all my working life" appears in this segment, it functions as a modifier for the action of doing the job. There are no spelling or syntax errors here.
 
• **No correction required** – Since there are no errors in subject-verb agreement, tense usage, or punctuation, this is the appropriate choice.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

"No sooner had she left the room when the lights went out."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the conjunction "**when**" in the third part of the sentence.
 
• The expression "**No sooner**" is a correlative conjunction that is always paired with "**than**," not "when."
 
• When a sentence begins with "No sooner," it requires **inversion**, where the auxiliary verb (had) comes before the subject (she). This part is correctly written as "**had she left**."
 
• To rectify the error, "when" must be replaced with "**than**" to complete the structure "No sooner... than."

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"No sooner had she left the room **than** the lights went out."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "No sooner"** – This is the correct starting phrase for indicating that one event happened immediately after another.
 
• **Option 2: "had she left"** – This maintains the necessary inversion (Auxiliary + Subject + Main Verb) for sentences starting with negative adverbs.
 
• **Option 4: "the lights went out"** – This is a grammatically correct clause in the simple past tense, describing the second action.
 
• **Confusing Pairs:** Remember that "**Hardly**," "**Scarcely**," and "**Barely**" are the words that are paired with "**when**." (e.g., *Hardly had she left the room **when** the lights went out.*)

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The phrase "**taken aback by**" is a standard expression used to indicate surprise or shock caused by something.
 
• The preposition "**by**" is the correct choice here, as it is commonly used with the verb "taken aback" to specify the cause of the surprise.
 
• Options **2 (at)**, **3 (for)**, and **4 (over)** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The manager was taken aback **by**__ the sudden resignation of three key employees."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "at"** is incorrect because "at" does not convey the correct relationship between the manager and the cause of surprise.
 
• **Option 3: "for"** is incorrect because it does not fit the standard usage of the phrase "taken aback."
 
• **Option 4: "over"** is incorrect because "over" does not work in this construction.
</ul

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence:

The students were imitating the way of the description by the teacher.

options.text: The way of the description by the teacher was imitated by the students.
The way of the description by the teacher were being imitated by the students.
The way of the description by the teacher had been imitated by the students.
The way of the description by the teacher was being imitated by the students.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The students were imitating the way of the description by the teacher."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the way of the description by the teacher" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "were imitating" to "was being imitated" (past continuous passive voice).
 
• Ensure the subject "the students" is preceded by the preposition "by" in the passive voice sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The way of the description by the teacher was being imitated by the students."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The way of the description by the teacher was imitated by the students." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"The way of the description by the teacher were being imitated by the students." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement (plural "were" is incorrect for singular "way").
 
• **Option 3: **"The way of the description by the teacher had been imitated by the students." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice:

All the arrangements had been made by the organizers before we arrived.

options.text: The organizers made all the arrangements before we arrived.
The organizers will have made all the arrangements before we arrive.
The organizers had made all the arrangements before we arrived.
The organizers have made all the arrangements before we arrived.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The given sentence is in passive voice: "All the arrangements had been made by the organizers before we arrived."
 
• To convert this sentence into active voice, the subject "the organizers" will be placed at the beginning.
 
• The verb "had been made" in passive voice changes to "had made" in active voice (past perfect tense).
 
• The object "all the arrangements" remains after the verb.
 
• The time clause "before we arrived" remains unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The organizers had made all the arrangements before we arrived."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The organizers made all the arrangements before we arrived." – Incorrect as it uses simple past instead of past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 2: **"The organizers will have made all the arrangements before we arrive." – Incorrect as it uses future perfect tense.
 
• **Option 4: **"The organizers have made all the arrangements before we arrived." – Incorrect as it uses present perfect tense instead of past perfect.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Snigdha said, "What a beautiful day today is!"

options.text: Snigdha exclaimed that that day has been a very beautiful day.
Snigdha exclaimed that that day a very beautiful day was.
Snigdha exclaimed that day was a very beautiful day.
Snigdha exclaimed that that day was a very beautiful day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Snigdha exclaimed that that day was a very beautiful day.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"What a beautiful day today is!" becomes "that day was a very beautiful day"**
 
 
• Exclamation is converted to a declarative sentence in indirect speech.
 
• Pronoun "today" changes to "that day" to reflect the perspective of indirect narration.
 
• Verb "is" changes to "was" to match the past tense required in reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: "said"
 
• Converted to: "exclaimed" to convey the emotional expression of the original exclamation.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Indirect speech does not use quotation marks.
 
• The sentence is structured with proper tense and pronoun changes to reflect the indirect narration.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Snigdha exclaimed that that day was a very beautiful day.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Snigdha exclaimed that that day has been a very beautiful day."

 
 
• Incorrect tense usage. "Has been" is present perfect, which does not match the past tense required in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Snigdha exclaimed that that day a very beautiful day was."
 
 
• Incorrect word order. The sentence structure is awkward and does not follow proper English grammar.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Snigdha exclaimed that day was a very beautiful day."
 
 
• Missing the pronoun "that" before "day," resulting in incomplete conversion.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech:

They asked if I knew the way to the museum.

options.text: They asked, "Do you know the way to the museum?"
They asked, "Did you know the way to the museum?"
They ask, "If I know the way to the museum?"
They said, "Did you know the way to the museum?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** They asked if I knew the way to the museum.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"They asked if I knew" becomes "Do you know"**
 
 
• Indirect question "if I knew" is converted to direct question "Do you know."
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "you" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "knew" is changed to "know" to match the present tense in direct questions.
 
 
 
• **"the way to the museum" remains the same**
 
 
• The object of the question does not change in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "They asked"
 
• Converted to: "They asked," maintaining the inquiry tone.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Do" and ends with a question mark "?".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They asked, “Do you know the way to the museum?”"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "They asked, ‘Did you know the way to the museum?’" 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "Did you know" implies a past inquiry, whereas the original sentence uses "knew" in a general sense.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "They ask, ‘If I know the way to the museum?’" 
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb: "They ask" changes the tense and does not match the original sentence.
 
• Incorrect word order: "If I know" is not proper direct speech format.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "They said, ‘Did you know the way to the museum?’" 
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb: "They said" changes the tone from a question to a statement.
 
• Incorrect tense: "Did you know" implies a past inquiry, altering the meaning.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

His fascination ______ mythology grew ______ exposure to ancient texts.
questions.solution:

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

• **Option 4: "at, under"** is incorrect as these prepositions do not fit the context of the sentence.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech:

He said that by the time she arrived, the guests had already started leaving.

options.text: He said, "By the time she has arrived, the guests were already leaving."
He said, "By the time she had arrived, the guests had already started leaving."
He said, "By the time she arrived, the guests had already started leaving."
He said, "By the time she arrived, the guests had already started to leave."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** In direct speech, the exact words of the speaker are enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"By the time she arrived, the guests had already started leaving" remains unchanged.**
 
 
• The original sentence uses the correct past tense "arrived" and "had already started leaving," which matches the grammatical structure of direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "He said that..."
 
• Converted to: "He said," followed by the quoted speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "By" and ends with a period inside the quotation marks.
 
• The reporting clause precedes the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He said, "By the time she arrived, the guests had already started leaving."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "By the time she has arrived, the guests were already leaving."
 
 
• Incorrect tense usage: "has arrived" is present perfect, which doesn't match the original sentence.
 
• "were already leaving" changes the meaning from "started leaving" to ongoing action.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "By the time she had arrived, the guests had already started leaving."
 
 
• Tense mismatch: "had arrived" implies an earlier past action than "arrived," which alters the timeline of events.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "By the time she arrived, the guests had already started to leave."
 
 
• "Started to leave" is acceptable but less natural than "started leaving" in this context.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

It was widely considered that the ancient ruins were believed to have been constructed by a previously unknown civilization.

options.text: They widely considered that a previously unknown civilization believed to have constructed the ancient ruins.
People widely considered that a previously unknown civilization was believed to have constructed the ancient ruins.
People widely considered that a previously unknown civilization had constructed the ancient ruins.
It was believed that a previously unknown civilization had constructed the ancient ruins, it was widely considered.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• To change the sentence from passive to active voice, the subject of the passive sentence must become the object in the active sentence. 
 
• In the given passive sentence, "It was widely considered that the ancient ruins were believed to have been constructed by a previously unknown civilization," the action centers around the belief of construction. 
 
• The active sentence must focus on "People" or "They," who considered or believed the construction of the ancient ruins. 
 
• The correct active voice structure should express the hypothetical situation of belief directly. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"People widely considered that a previously unknown civilization had constructed the ancient ruins."*

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

Bob was drawing the portrait.

options.text: The portrait is being drawn by Bob.
The portrait was being drawn by Bob.
The portrait has been drawn by Bob.
The portrait was drawn by Bob.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Bob was drawing the portrait."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the portrait" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "was drawing" to "was being drawn" (past continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Bob."
 
• Ensure the sentence retains its original meaning and tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The portrait was being drawn by Bob."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The portrait is being drawn by Bob." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).
 
• **Option 3:** "The portrait has been drawn by Bob." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4:** "The portrait was drawn by Bob." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).

questions.question:
"From childhood, Japanese people are taught to respect rules, value punctuality, and prioritise community welfare over individual interests."

What is the **part of speech** of the word **"punctuality"?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3 (Noun)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Verb***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Punctuality” does not denote an action; it names a quality.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Adjective***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adjective form is “punctual,” not “punctuality.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Noun***
 
 
• This is **correct**. “Punctuality” is a noun that refers to the quality or state of being punctual (on time). In the sentence, it functions as the object of the verb “value.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Adverb***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adverb form would be “punctually,” not “punctuality.”
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3 (Noun)**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Punctuality** is derived from the adjective *punctual* + suffix *-ity*, which forms abstract nouns denoting qualities.
 
• Examples: “responsible → responsibility,” “active → activity.”
 
• In the passage, “value punctuality” means to appreciate or respect the quality of being on time.

questions.question:
"The Japanese education system also strongly focuses on moral training, teamwork, and responsibility,"

why is the verb** "focuses"** used instead of **"focus"**?

options.text: Because the sentence is in passive voice

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2 (Because "system" is a singular subject)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Because "training" is the object***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The verb form is determined by the subject, not the object. “Training” is the object of the verb “focuses.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Because "system" is a singular subject***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The subject of the sentence is “The Japanese education system,” which is singular. Therefore, the verb must agree in the singular form: “focuses.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Because "education" is uncountable***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While “education” is uncountable, the subject is “system,” not “education.” The verb agreement depends on “system.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Because the sentence is in passive voice***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The sentence is in active voice (“system focuses”), not passive. Passive would be “is focused on.”
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**: *Because "system" is a singular subject.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Subject-verb agreement rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb form (with -s or -es in present tense).
 
• Example: “The committee **decides** the rules.” / “The system **works** efficiently.”
 
• If the subject were plural (“systems”), the verb would be “focus.”
